Your First Five Minutes with tampaBayOpenData

Source: vignettes/first-five-minutes.Rmd
first-five-minutes.Rmd

Find parks data and make a bar chart in base R.

Use 100 Hillsborough County property records saved on October 24, 2026, or fetch current records in step 3. The saved example works offline after installation.

1. Install and load

Install once:

install.packages("tampaBayOpenData")

Load in each R session:

library(tampaBayOpenData)

2. Find a dataset

Search the offline catalog:

matches <- tbod_search_datasets("parks", source = "checked")
matches[, c("canonical_id", "publisher", "title")]
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>   canonical_id             publisher              title                         
#>   <chr>                    <chr>                  <chr>                         
#> 1 tampa-parks              City of Tampa          Park polygons                 
#> 2 hillsborough-parks       Hillsborough County    Hillsborough County parks and…
#> 3 st-pete-parks            City of St. Petersburg St. Petersburg parks          
#> 4 clearwater-park-buffers  City of Clearwater     Clearwater park buffers       
#> 5 pinellas-park-boundaries Pinellas County        Pinellas County park boundari…
#> 6 pinellas-trail           Pinellas County        Pinellas Trail segments

Use the hillsborough-parks ID below.

3. Load data

Choose one option.

Saved preview

Load the bundled data offline:

parks_file <- system.file("extdata", "parks-preview.rds",
                          package = "tampaBayOpenData", mustWork = TRUE)
parks <- readRDS(parks_file)

Current records

With internet access, request up to 100 records:

parks <- tbod_get_dataset("hillsborough-parks", limit = 100)

These are the first records returned, not a random sample. One park may have several property records.

Knitting this file uses the saved preview. Run the live request yourself to use current data.

4. Summarize

Check the first rows, row count, and column names:

head(parks[, c("NAME", "TYPE", "USES")])
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>   NAME                        TYPE  USES           
#>   <chr>                       <chr> <chr>          
#> 1 Alafia River Boat Ramp      L     Boat Ramp      
#> 2 Alexander                   L     Programmed     
#> 3 All People's Life Center    L     Community      
#> 4 Clayton                     L     Sports         
#> 5 Antioch                     L     Sports         
#> 6 Apollo Beach and Skate Park L     SportsRec_Skate
nrow(parks)
#> [1] 100
names(parks)
#>  [1] "OBJECTID_1"       "FOLIONUMB"        "NAME"             "ADDR"            
#>  [5] "TYPE"             "USES"             "PROPOWNER"        "PROPMNG"         
#>  [9] "GlobalID"         "created_user"     "created_date"     "last_edited_user"
#> [13] "last_edited_date" "Shape__Area"      "Shape__Length"

Count the USES labels:

uses <- trimws(parks$USES)
uses[is.na(uses) | uses == ""] <- "Not reported"
park_uses <- table(uses)
park_uses <- sort(park_uses, decreasing = TRUE)
park_uses
#> uses
#>            Sports            Nature        Playground        Recreation 
#>                24                16                14                14 
#>            Office   SportsRec_Skate         Boat Ramp         Community 
#>                 8                 7                 3                 3 
#>        Programmed               Dog Sports_Recreation            Trails 
#>                 3                 2                 2                 2 
#>        Equestrian       Maintenance 
#>                 1                 1

Blank or missing labels are grouped as “Not reported”.

5. Make a chart

Plot the five most common labels:

top_uses <- head(park_uses, 5)
par(mar = c(4, 10, 3, 1))
if (length(top_uses) > 0) {
  barplot(rev(top_uses), horiz = TRUE, las = 1, cex.names = 0.8,
        col = "steelblue", xlab = "Property records",
        main = "Most common uses in this preview")
} else {
  plot.new()
  text(0.5, 0.5, "No property records returned")
}

Sports leads the saved preview, followed by Nature. Current results may differ.

The bars count property records in this preview, not unique parks across the county. Map outlines do not confirm boundaries, access, or opening hours.

If a live request fails or reports changed column names, see the retrieval troubleshooting guide.

Data: Hillsborough County Parks and Recreation properties, used under CC BY 4.0.
